verdictReason: All 15 round-1 findings are genuinely addressed, including both HIGHs. CRIT-2 holds against the code: live Save persists contextDigest via AuthoringRevisionIdentity.create in StudioService.storeAuthoring, and the digest covers ordered (id,text), the globalContext hash, every whole-step-context hash, nonsecret value hashes and evidence. CRIT-5 holds: the V21 trigger overwrites NEW.authoring unconditionally, and trg_ui_test_revision_capture fires first by name order, so V26 (d)+(e) is the right fix. The revision introduced new defects, though. In the Q2 creation transaction, Q1's write-once outcome is inserted as ESCALATED_FULL before the preconditions are checked, which contradicts the later 'instead written as DISCARDED'. Q2's plan is unspecified: the 'normal capture path' re-runs the planner, which would hit rule 4a and label Q2 PRIOR_ESCALATION. The B1 capture-for-all scope misses the live v1 publish path, publishAcceptedCandidate -> insertOrReuseRevision, which bypasses captured insertion entirely. These are bounded spec-text fixes. There are no HIGH issues, and the weighted score is 3.98.

ungatedCaptureAssessment.rationale: The AUTO-DECISION reasoning holds. V19 requires every replica to capture every compile. The V26 schema parts cannot be flagged. After V19, a flag-off replica would fail publication (the require-request trigger), so a flag would be a trap rather than a kill switch. Before V19, redeploying the pre-B1 binary is a valid rollback. Ungated is acceptable only if B1 is complete and its rollback claim is tested.
conditions: 1. B1 must switch EVERY live publish path to captured insertion, naming publishAcceptedCandidate (CompilePipeline:266 -> insertOrReuseRevision, CompileStateService:273) as well as publishCandidate. The v1 publish-and-accept semantics (READY without a separate confirm) stay unchanged. Today's spec text does not cover this path (CRIT-18).

2. Capture for unversioned (v1) callers must add no new rejection mode. An absent or invalid V21 pair is captured as stored and plans FULL LEGACY_MAPPING, never 409. The InferenceCaptureStore.persist 'Authoring snapshot differs from captured source' IllegalStateException is rebased or cannot fire on this path (CRIT-19).

3. The rollback claim is tested, not asserted. The pre-B1 binary's backend IT suite passes against a schema with V26 applied (the whole-row trigger and the extended consistency trigger), in addition to the new binary's full suite.

4. V19 is not part of B1's deploy. B1 runs on all replicas before the separate V19 runbook step, and the runbook has a go/no-go that compares compile error/STALE rates before and after B1 (no numeric target invented; the comparison is the gate).
5. The B1 story header and PR description carry 'LIVE-AFFECTING, not dark' so that the @devops pre-push review treats it as a live change.

issues.description: The Q2 creation step order contradicts write-once outcomes. §3.2.5 step 2 inserts Q1's outcome as ESCALATED_FULL in (a), checks the preconditions in (b), and in (d) says Q1's outcome 'is instead written as DISCARDED'. ui_test_compile_outcomes is append-only and recordOutcome uses ON CONFLICT(request_id) DO NOTHING, so the DISCARDED write after (a) is silently dropped. An implementer following the text records ESCALATED_FULL with no Q2. The Run gate then sees ESCALATED_FULL, finds no escalatedTo, and cannot reach the specified 'stops, asks to Run again' state.
issues.suggestion: Reorder step 2: (a) check the preconditions; (b) insert exactly ONE Q1 outcome, ESCALATED_FULL if they hold, otherwise DISCARDED with its reasonDetail; (c) capture Q2 only in the ESCALATED_FULL branch. Add to EscalationCreationIT: in the DISCARDED case, Q1 has exactly one outcome row and it is DISCARDED.

issues.description: Q2's plan is asserted, not derived. Step 2(c) says Q2 is captured 'through the normal capture path' with selectedMode FULL / reason PREFIX_IMPACT. The normal path (capture -> InferenceCaptureStore.persist) runs the planner. With Q1's ESCALATED_FULL outcome already inserted in the same transaction, rule 4a fires, so Q2 gets reasonDetail PRIOR_ESCALATION and escalation.source=PRIOR_ESCALATION. That contradicts AC-8 and skews escalationRate by source. If instead requestedMode FULL is passed, the reason becomes EXPLICIT_FULL. Separately, the 'normal capture path' entry point captureForCompilation is REQUIRES_NEW, which would break step 2's single-transaction atomicity. Only capture (@Transactional, joins) preserves it.
issues.suggestion: State that Q2 is captured via the joining CompileStateService.capture with an explicit plan override {selectedMode FULL, reason PREFIX_IMPACT, escalation.source MODEL, escalatedFrom Q1} that bypasses the planner, and that rule 4a applies only to user-initiated compiles (escalated_from_request_id IS NULL). Add a unit/IT assertion: Q2.plan.escalation.source = MODEL, not PRIOR_ESCALATION.

issues.description: Capture-for-all misses the live publish path. The live compile publishes through CompilePipeline:266 -> CompileStateService.publishAcceptedCandidate, which unconditionally calls insertOrReuseRevision (:273). Only publishCandidate branches to insertCapturedRevision. The spec's B1 ('captured publication writes the V21/V24 columns', §5.2 CompileStateService row) never names publishAcceptedCandidate. Left unchanged, v1 revisions bypass V26 (a)/(e), and once V19's require-request trigger is applied every live v1 compile fails at publication, which is exactly the COL-4 outage the sequencing is meant to prevent.
issues.suggestion: In §3.2.3/§5.2 and the §9 B1 scope, list both publish paths and require that publishAcceptedCandidate use captured insertion (keeping its publish-and-accept semantics). Add to the capture-for-all IT: a v1 compile produces a revision with non-null compile_request_id whose V21/V24 columns equal its request's.

issues.description: §3.2.1 defines 409 STALE_REVISION only for versioned capture with an invalid V21 pair. Nothing says what capture-for-all does for v1 callers whose V21 pair is absent (legacy) or fails AuthoringRevisionIdentity.valid, or when InferenceCaptureStore.persist's 'Authoring snapshot differs from captured source' guard trips. Any of these could turn today's working v1 compile into a new failure on the ungated live path.
issues.suggestion: Add: 'For unversioned callers, capture never rejects on authoring identity. It stores the V21 columns as found (possibly NULL) and plans FULL LEGACY_MAPPING. The persist text/snapshot guard is rebased to V21 or skipped for this path.' Add one IT row.

issues.description: Three small claims do not match the code. (a) 'The existing abandonment sweeper settles Q1 as retryable STALE': sweepAbandoned only resets ui_tests and writes no outcome row, so Q1 stays unsettled. This fails safe for rule 4a, but GET /compiles/{Q1} must render it. (b) 'A second insert fails and the existing Q2 is returned': in PostgreSQL a failed INSERT aborts the transaction, so idempotency needs INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (escalated_from_request_id) DO NOTHING followed by a select. (c) Rule 4a's key authoringHash includes nonsecret value hashes, so a value-only edit reopens INCREMENTAL once. That fails safe at the cost of one wasted Q1, and should be stated.
issues.suggestion: Reword (a) to 'the sweeper returns the draft to STALE; Q1 has no outcome row and the compile resource reports it as abandoned'. Specify ON CONFLICT for (b). Add a one-line note for (c).
